front: Quem não tem cão caça com gato: sem o projetor, usamos a parede branca mesmo.
pronunciation: KENG NOWNG teng KOWNG KAH-sah kohng GAH-too: seng oo proh-zheh-TOHR, oo-ZAH-mooz ah pah-REH-jee BRAHN-kah MEHZ-moo.
back: If you don't have a dog, you hunt with a cat: without the projector, we just used the white wall.
context: Make do with what you have. The original was probably 'caça como gato' (hunts like a cat, alone), later reinterpreted as 'com gato'.

front: De grão em grão, a galinha enche o papo.
pronunciation: jee GROWNG eng GROWNG, ah gah-LEE-nyah EHN-shee oo PAH-poo.
back: Grain by grain, the hen fills her crop.
context: Little by little you reach your goal. Often said about saving money or learning a language!

front: Água mole em pedra dura tanto bate até que fura.
pronunciation: AH-gwah MOH-lee eng PEH-drah DOO-rah TAHN-too BAH-chee ah-TEH keh FOO-rah.
back: Soft water on hard stone keeps hitting until it makes a hole.
context: Persistence wins in the end. Similar to 'constant dripping wears away the stone'.

front: A cavalo dado não se olham os dentes.
pronunciation: ah kah-VAH-loo DAH-doo NOWNG see OH-lyowngz oos DEHN-chees.
back: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.
context: Don't criticize a gift. Often heard as 'cavalo dado não se olha os dentes'; the version with 'a' and the plural verb is the grammatically careful one.

front: Em casa de ferreiro, o espeto é de pau.
pronunciation: eng KAH-zah jee feh-RRAY-roo, oo ehs-PEH-too EH jee POW.
back: In the blacksmith's house, the skewer is made of wood.
context: Professionals neglect their own needs: the dentist with bad teeth, the IT person whose laptop never works.

front: Cão que ladra não morde.
pronunciation: KOWNG keh LAH-drah NOWNG MOHR-jee.
back: A barking dog doesn't bite.
context: People who make loud threats rarely act on them. 'Ladrar' = to bark (also 'latir', more common in speech).

front: Quem semeia vento colhe tempestade.
pronunciation: KENG seh-MAY-ah VEHN-too KOH-lyee tehm-pehs-TAH-jee.
back: Whoever sows the wind reaps the storm.
context: Biblical origin (Hosea). Bad actions bring worse consequences.

front: A pressa é inimiga da perfeição.
pronunciation: ah PREH-sah EH ee-nee-MEE-gah dah pehr-fay-SOWNG.
back: Haste is the enemy of perfection.
context: Said to someone rushing a job. Similar to 'haste makes waste'.

front: O hábito não faz o monge.
pronunciation: oo AH-bee-too NOWNG FAHZ oo MOHN-zhee.
back: The habit doesn't make the monk.
context: Wordplay: 'hábito' = habit (routine) and the monk's robe. Don't judge by appearances.

front: Pimenta nos olhos dos outros é refresco.
pronunciation: pee-MEHN-tah nooz OH-lyooz dooz OH-troos EH rreh-FREHS-koo.
back: Pepper in other people's eyes is refreshing.
context: It's easy to make light of problems that aren't yours. Said to someone who downplays your suffering.

front: Macaco velho não põe a mão em cumbuca.
pronunciation: mah-KAH-koo VEH-lyoo NOWNG POYNG ah MOWNG eng koom-BOO-kah.
back: An old monkey doesn't put its hand in a gourd.
context: Experienced people don't fall into traps. Monkeys were caught by gourds with food they couldn't pull their fist out of.

front: Quem vê cara não vê coração.
pronunciation: KENG VEH KAH-rah NOWNG VEH koh-rah-SOWNG.
back: Whoever sees a face doesn't see the heart.
context: You can't know someone's true character from their looks.

front: Deus ajuda quem cedo madruga.
pronunciation: DEH-ooz ah-ZHOO-dah KENG SEH-doo mah-DROO-gah.
back: God helps those who get up early.
context: Equivalent to 'the early bird catches the worm'. Brazilians often joke: 'mas quem madruga dorme à tarde'.

front: Cada macaco no seu galho.
pronunciation: KAH-dah mah-KAH-koo noo SEH-oo GAH-lyoo.
back: Each monkey on its own branch.
context: Mind your own business / everyone should stick to their own role.

front: Falar é fácil; fazer é que são elas.
pronunciation: fah-LAHR EH FAH-seel; fah-ZEHR EH keh SOWNG EH-lahs.
back: Talking is easy; doing is the hard part.
context: 'É que são elas' (that's where the trouble lies) is a fixed expression for the difficult part.

front: A corda sempre arrebenta do lado mais fraco.
pronunciation: ah KOHR-dah SEHM-pree ah-rreh-BEHN-tah doo LAH-doo MAHYS FRAH-koo.
back: The rope always breaks on the weakest side.
context: The most vulnerable always suffer the consequences, e.g. junior staff when a company cuts costs.

front: Santo de casa não faz milagre.
pronunciation: SAHN-too jee KAH-zah NOWNG FAHZ mee-LAH-gree.
back: A saint at home performs no miracles.
context: People don't value talent close to them; similar to 'no one is a prophet in their own land'.

front: Onde há fumaça, há fogo.
pronunciation: OHN-jee AH foo-MAH-sah, AH FOH-goo.
back: Where there's smoke, there's fire.
context: Rumors usually have some truth behind them. Same idea as in English.

front: O peixe morre pela boca.
pronunciation: oo PAY-shee MOH-rree PEH-lah BOH-kah.
back: The fish dies by its mouth.
context: People get into trouble by talking too much (or, literally, by eating too much).

front: Quem não chora não mama.
pronunciation: KENG NOWNG SHOH-rah NOWNG MAH-mah.
back: Whoever doesn't cry doesn't get fed.
context: If you don't ask or complain, you don't get anything. Similar to 'the squeaky wheel gets the grease'.

front: A mentira tem perna curta.
pronunciation: ah mehn-CHEE-rah teng PEHR-nah KOOR-tah.
back: Lies have short legs.
context: Lies don't get far: they are found out quickly.

front: Nem tanto ao mar, nem tanto à terra.
pronunciation: NENG TAHN-too ah-oo MAHR, NENG TAHN-too AH TEH-rrah.
back: Neither too much toward the sea, nor too much toward the land.
context: Keep to the middle ground; avoid extremes. Note the crase in 'à terra'.

front: Vamos dar nome aos bois: quem atrasou o projeto foi o fornecedor.
pronunciation: VAH-mooz DAHR NOH-mee ah-ooz BOYS: KENG ah-trah-ZOH oo proh-ZHEH-too FOY oo fohr-neh-seh-DOHR.
back: Let's call a spade a spade: it was the supplier who delayed the project.
context: 'Dar nome aos bois' (to name the oxen) = to say clearly who is responsible.

front: Mais vale um pássaro na mão do que dois voando.
pronunciation: MAHYZ VAH-lee oong PAH-sah-roo nah MOWNG doo keh DOYZ voh-AHN-doo.
back: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
context: Same image as the English proverb, but the birds are 'flying' instead of 'in the bush'.

front: Quando o calo apertou, ninguém quis pagar o pato.
pronunciation: KWAHN-doo oo KAH-loo ah-pehr-TOH, neen-GENG KEES pah-GAHR oo PAH-too.
back: When things got tough, nobody wanted to take the blame.
context: 'Pagar o pato' = to take the blame for others, probably from an old tale of a man left to pay for a duck. 'Quando o calo aperta' = when the going gets tough.

front: Ele chorou lágrimas de crocodilo no velório do sócio.
pronunciation: EH-lee shoh-ROH LAH-gree-mahz jee kroh-koh-JEE-loo noo veh-LOH-ryoo doo SOH-syoo.
back: He cried crocodile tears at his business partner's wake.
context: 'Lágrimas de crocodilo' = fake tears, exactly as in English. 'Velório' = wake.

front: Depois da terceira derrota seguida, a vaca foi para o brejo.
pronunciation: deh-POYZ dah tehr-SAY-rah deh-RROH-tah seh-GEE-dah, ah VAH-kah FOY PAH-rah oo BREH-zhoo.
back: After the third defeat in a row, everything went down the drain.
context: 'A vaca foi pro brejo' (the cow went into the swamp) = things went completely wrong.

front: Não cutuque a onça com vara curta.
pronunciation: NOWNG koo-TOO-kee ah OHN-sah kohng VAH-rah KOOR-tah.
back: Don't poke the jaguar with a short stick.
context: Don't provoke someone dangerous or powerful. 'Onça' = jaguar, a very Brazilian image.

front: Você é um amigo da onça: contou meu segredo para todo mundo!
pronunciation: voh-SEH EH oong ah-MEE-goo dah OHN-sah: kohn-TOH MEH-oo seh-GREH-doo PAH-rah TOH-doo MOON-doo!
back: Some friend you are: you told my secret to everybody!
context: 'Amigo da onça' = a false friend, from a famous 1940s cartoon character in the magazine O Cruzeiro.

front: Ele resolveu o problema, mas fez questão de matar a cobra e mostrar o pau.
pronunciation: EH-lee rreh-zohl-VEH-oo oo proh-BLEH-mah, mahs FEHS kehs-TOWNG jee mah-TAHR ah KOH-brah ee mohs-TRAHR oo POW.
back: He solved the problem, but made a point of showing the proof.
context: 'Matar a cobra e mostrar o pau' (kill the snake and show the stick) = to back up a claim with evidence.

front: Hoje a chefe está com a macaca; melhor não pedir nada.
pronunciation: OH-zhee ah SHEH-fee ehs-TAH kohng ah mah-KAH-kah; meh-LYOHR NOWNG peh-JEER NAH-dah.
back: The boss is in a terrible mood today; better not ask for anything.
context: 'Estar com a macaca' (to be with the female monkey) = to be in a foul or agitated mood. Very colloquial.

front: Ele vai devolver o dinheiro quando as galinhas tiverem dentes.
pronunciation: EH-lee VAHY deh-vohl-VEHR oo jee-NYAY-roo KWAHN-doo ahz gah-LEE-nyahs chee-VEH-reng DEHN-chees.
back: He'll pay the money back when hens have teeth.
context: Equivalent to 'when pigs fly'. Note the future subjunctive 'tiverem' after 'quando'.

front: Meu avô dorme com as galinhas e acorda às cinco.
pronunciation: MEH-oo ah-VOH DOHR-mee kohng ahz gah-LEE-nyahz ee ah-KOHR-dah AHS SEEN-koo.
back: My grandfather goes to bed very early and wakes up at five.
context: 'Dormir com as galinhas' = to go to bed at sunset, like hens.

front: Esse trabalho é muita areia para o meu caminhãozinho.
pronunciation: EH-see trah-BAH-lyoo EH MOOY-tah ah-RAY-ah PAH-rah oo MEH-oo kah-mee-nyowng-ZEE-nyoo.
back: This job is way out of my league.
context: 'Muita areia pro meu caminhãozinho' (too much sand for my little truck) = more than I can handle, or someone out of my league romantically.

front: Ela passou a aula inteira pensando na morte da bezerra.
pronunciation: EH-lah pah-SOH ah OW-lah een-TAY-rah pehn-SAHN-doo nah MOHR-chee dah beh-ZEH-rrah.
back: She spent the whole class daydreaming.
context: 'Pensar na morte da bezerra' (to think about the calf's death) = to be lost in thought, absent-minded.

front: Mudar o nome do departamento é trocar seis por meia dúzia.
pronunciation: moo-DAHR oo NOH-mee doo deh-pahr-tah-MEHN-too EH troh-KAHR SAYS pohr MAY-ah DOO-zyah.
back: Renaming the department is six of one, half a dozen of the other.
context: 'Trocar seis por meia dúzia' = a change that changes nothing.

front: Pode chover canivetes: amanhã eu vou à praia.
pronunciation: POH-jee shoh-VEHR kah-nee-VEH-chees: ah-mah-NYAH EH-oo VOH AH PRAHY-ah.
back: Come hell or high water, I'm going to the beach tomorrow.
context: 'Chover canivetes' (to rain pocketknives) = whatever happens. Also used for very heavy rain.

front: Essa desculpa é conversa para boi dormir.
pronunciation: EH-sah jehs-KOOL-pah EH kohn-VEHR-sah PAH-rah BOY dohr-MEER.
back: That excuse is a load of nonsense.
context: 'Conversa pra boi dormir' (talk to make the ox sleep) = boring or untrue talk meant to fool you.

front: Pintaram a sala de uma cor de burro quando foge.
pronunciation: peen-TAH-rowng ah SAH-lah jee OO-mah KOHR jee BOO-rroo KWAHN-doo FOH-zhee.
back: They painted the living room some indescribable color.
context: 'Cor de burro quando foge' (the color of a fleeing donkey) = an ugly, hard-to-define color. Humorous.

front: O novo escritório fica onde Judas perdeu as botas.
pronunciation: oo NOH-voo ehs-kree-TOH-ryoo FEE-kah OHN-jee ZHOO-dahs pehr-DEH-oo ahz BOH-tahs.
back: The new office is in the middle of nowhere.
context: 'Onde Judas perdeu as botas' = a remote, hard-to-reach place.

front: Com o salário atrasado, tivemos que fazer das tripas coração.
pronunciation: kohng oo sah-LAH-ryoo ah-trah-ZAH-doo, chee-VEH-mooz keh fah-ZEHR dahs TREE-pahs koh-rah-SOWNG.
back: With our salary late, we had to go to extraordinary lengths to get by.
context: 'Fazer das tripas coração' (make a heart out of guts) = to make a huge effort despite difficulties.

front: Com esse orçamento, vamos ter que tirar leite de pedra.
pronunciation: kohng EH-see ohr-sah-MEHN-too, VAH-mooz TEHR keh chee-RAHR LAY-chee jee PEH-drah.
back: With this budget, we'll have to squeeze blood from a stone.
context: 'Tirar leite de pedra' (to get milk from a stone) = to achieve results with almost no resources.

front: A estratégia deles é deixar o gato subir no telhado antes de dar a má notícia.
pronunciation: ah ehs-trah-TEH-zhyah DEH-leez EH day-SHAHR oo GAH-too soo-BEER noo teh-LYAH-doo AHN-cheez jee DAHR ah MAH noh-CHEE-syah.
back: Their strategy is to prepare people gently before breaking the bad news.
context: From a joke: instead of 'your cat died', say 'the cat climbed onto the roof…' first. Preparing someone for bad news.

front: Ele tem memória de elefante: lembra o nome de todos os clientes.
pronunciation: EH-lee teng meh-MOH-ryah jee eh-leh-FAHN-chee: LEHM-brah oo NOH-mee jee TOH-dooz ooz klee-EHN-chees.
back: He has a memory like an elephant: he remembers every client's name.
context: 'Memória de elefante' = an excellent memory. Note 'lembrar algo' (no 'de') when there's no reflexive pronoun.

front: Parece uma mosca-morta, mas é a mais esperta do grupo.
pronunciation: pah-REH-see OO-mah MOHS-kah-MOHR-tah, mahz EH ah MAHYZ ehs-PEHR-tah doo GROO-poo.
back: She seems like a meek little thing, but she's the smartest in the group.
context: 'Mosca-morta' (dead fly) = someone who seems passive or harmless, sometimes hiding cunning.
